name: Congenital Communicating Hydrocephalus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Communicating Hydrocephalus

criteria.description: Enlargement of the cerebral ventricles on neuroimaging without evidence of obstruction
Presence of signs of increased intracranial pressure such as bulging fontanelle, rapid head circumference growth
Demonstration of patent cerebrospinal fluid pathways on imaging studies (e.g., MRI or CT cisternography)
Exclusion of obstructive hydrocephalus causes such as aqueductal stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ventriculomegaly with clinical signs of increased intracranial pressure and patent CSF pathways on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of obstructive causes and may be supported by CSF dynamics studies.

bulging soft spot on baby's head

common.symptomName: Vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: throwing up due to increased intracranial pressure

rare.symptomName: Bradycardia secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: slow heart rate from brain pressure
bradycardia linked to raised intracranial pressure
reduced heartbeat due to brain swelling

laboratory: Elevated opening pressure on lumbar puncture (if performed)
imaging: Enlarged lateral, third, and fourth ventricles on MRI or CT without obstruction
Patent aqueduct of Sylvius and basal cisterns on MRI
Absence of mass lesions or hemorrhage
other: Increased head circumference crossing percentiles on growth charts
Delayed myelination on neuroimaging in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Obstructive hydrocephalus with aqueductal narrowing on imaging
Absence of communication between third and fourth ventricles
Focal cystic lesion causing mass effect on ventricles
Ventricular enlargement secondary to brain atrophy

redFlags: Rapid head circumference increase crossing multiple percentiles
Bulging fontanelle with tense anterior fontanelle
Signs of brain herniation such as abnormal posturing or apnea
references: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology, 11th Edition
